title: Lafayette Theatre pit shows; learning to smoke
summary: He lived across from the Lafayette, played weekly shows and describes the show format.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And I was known around the Lafayette Theatre because I lived right across the street there at 158 West, on 31st. And the stage manager knew me. And whenever I wanted to, I could come in there and play a show because they changed shows every week, a different show.
Do you remember some of the shows?
Do you remember some of those shows?

Well, it was the same -- it followed the same pattern all the time. They weren't like the big shows on Broadway. It just just the head man and head lady, and you had ten chorus girls, and you'd do the kickups and all like that, and they'd do their numbers, and then you'd have two comedians who'd come on, and like that.

And that's how I learned how to smoke, being in the pit, because when the comedians would come on, they were on for about ten or 15 minutes, they did their part. You'd go out of the pit and go down there and grab a smoke, see. And til

this day I don't smoke cigars, I don't smoke cigarettes. And you find very few trumpet players smoke cigars. Smoke a cigarette, but not a cigar, because most cigars -- they keep the cigar in their mouth, they're talking and all that.
